newsitem.title: PERU: Freed Peruvian hostage thought warning was a joke.
newsitem.headline: Freed Peruvian hostage thought warning was a joke.

text.p: When a fellow hostage sidled up to Father Juan Julio Wicht in the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima to warn him they were about to be freed, the Jesuit priest thought it was just another joke to ease the tension.
"I was sitting there and they came up to me and said: 'They're going to free us in a few minutes. Stay calm'," Wicht told Peru's Panamericana television network on Wednesday.
"So I thought it was a joke, because we made lots of black jokes," added Wicht, who turned down a chance for freedom with 225 hostages released in December.
Crack Peruvian troops rescued 71 hostages in the surprise attack staged on the 126th day of the standoff.
Freed Bolivian Ambassador Jorge Gumucio said word was passed around the hostages about 10 minutes beforehand that a military assault was imminent.
One hostage, a Supreme Court justice, two soldiers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died.
